g: Apposition in a letter opening
In ‘Pablo, apóstol de Cristo Jesús’, the comma-set noun phrase identifies Pablo; the following ‘a los santos’ names the recipients.
e: por la voluntad de Dios
This fixed prepositional phrase means ‘by the will of God’; por presents God's will as the basis of Paul's commission.

g: Que + present subjunctive for a wish
‘Que Dios nuestro Padre y el Señor Jesucristo les concedan’ expresses a blessing: ‘May ... grant you.’ Concedan is plural because two coordinated subjects follow.
e: gracia y paz
The paired greeting combines gracia, undeserved favor, with paz, well-being and wholeness; both are the objects of concedan.

g: Alabado sea: benedictive word order
‘Alabado sea Dios’ places the participle before subjunctive sea to form the formal blessing ‘Praised be God,’ rather than a factual passive statement.
e: en las regiones celestiales
The phrase means ‘in the heavenly realms.’ Regiones is plural in this recurring Ephesians expression, and celestiales agrees with it.

g: para que + present subjunctive
In ‘para que seamos santos’, para que introduces God's purpose and therefore takes subjunctive seamos: ‘so that we may be holy.’
e: antes de la creación del mundo
A time phrase meaning ‘before the creation of the world.’ Antes de is followed here by a noun phrase, not a conjugated clause.

g: Object pronoun + preterite + para ser
‘Nos predestinó para ser adoptados’ means ‘he predestined us to be adopted.’ Nos is the object, and para ser introduces the intended result in the passive.
e: según el buen propósito de su voluntad
Según means ‘according to’ or ‘in keeping with.’ The phrase locates the decision in the good purpose of God's will.

g: Relative clause with que
In ‘la gracia, que nos concedió’, que refers back to gracia. The indirect object nos marks the people to whom that grace was granted.
e: su gloriosa gracia
Gloriosa modifies gracia and means ‘glorious’ or ‘splendid.’ The phrase is the object of the preceding purpose expression para alabanza de.

g: Apposition specifies redención
‘La redención ..., el perdón de nuestros pecados’ places two noun phrases together, so the second explains what redemption entails in this sentence.
e: mediante su sangre
Mediante is a formal preposition meaning ‘through’ or ‘by means of.’ Here the means of redemption is Christ's blood.

g: Relative que with an omitted antecedent nearby
‘Que Dios nos dio en abundancia’ continues the description of gracia from the preceding verse; que functions as the object that God gave abundantly.
e: con toda sabiduría y entendimiento
Con introduces accompanying manner: God's abundant giving is associated with complete sabiduría and entendimiento, two coordinated abstract nouns.

g: Hacer + infinitive causative
‘Nos hizo conocer’ literally says ‘he made us know’ and idiomatically means ‘he made known to us.’ The object pronoun nos precedes hizo.
e: conforme al buen propósito
Conforme a means ‘in accordance with.’ The contraction al combines a + el before the masculine noun propósito.

v: to carry it out; accomplish it
g: Cuando + imperfect subjunctive
‘Cuando se cumpliera el tiempo’ uses cumpliera for an anticipated time viewed from a past plan; it means ‘when the time should be fulfilled.’
e: tanto las del cielo como las de la tierra
Tanto ... como pairs two parallel groups: ‘both those in heaven and those on earth.’ Las stands for the feminine plural cosas.

g: Ser + participle passive
‘Fuimos hechos herederos’ is a preterite passive: fuimos supplies past tense and hechos agrees with the plural subject nosotros.
e: aquel que hace todas las cosas
Aquel is a demonstrative pronoun meaning ‘the one.’ The relative clause que hace todas las cosas identifies whom it refers to.

g: Purpose clause with seamos
‘A fin de que ... seamos’ requires the present subjunctive because it states a purpose. The embedded relative ‘que ya hemos puesto’ modifies nosotros.
e: hemos puesto nuestra esperanza en Cristo
Poner la esperanza en is the natural collocation ‘to place one's hope in.’ The perfect tense presents that trust as already established.

v: seal; mark of ownership or authentication
g: Cuando + coordinated preterites
‘Cuando oyeron ... y lo creyeron’ gives two completed actions before the main passive ‘fueron marcados.’ Lo refers to the message or gospel heard.
e: fueron marcados con el sello
This passive means ‘were marked with the seal.’ In the ancient world a seal authenticated ownership; the verse identifies that seal as the promised Holy Spirit.

g: Hasta que + present subjunctive
‘Hasta que llegue la redención final’ uses subjunctive llegue because the endpoint is still future: ‘until final redemption arrives.’
e: pueblo adquirido por Dios
Adquirido por Dios is a reduced passive phrase: ‘a people acquired by God.’ Por introduces the agent of adquirido.

g: Enterarse de + noun
In ‘me enteré de la fe ... y del amor,’ enterarse requires de. Del is the contraction de + el before amor.
e: por mi parte
This discourse phrase means ‘for my part’ or ‘as for me.’ It marks Paul's own response to the report he has received.

g: No dejar de + infinitive
‘No he dejado de dar gracias’ literally means ‘I have not ceased giving thanks.’ The negative construction conveys continuous action.
e: al recordarlos en mis oraciones
Al + infinitive means ‘when’ or ‘as.’ In recordarlos, los is attached to the infinitive and refers to the recipients.

g: Pedir que + present subjunctive
‘Pido que ... les dé’ uses subjunctive dé because pedir introduces a request. The written accent distinguishes dé from the preposition de.
e: para que lo conozcan mejor
Para que introduces the desired purpose. Lo is the masculine direct-object pronoun, and conozcan is the ustedes subjunctive of conocer.

g: Subjunctive passive with les
‘Que les sean iluminados los ojos’ is a requested passive: sean + iluminados. Les identifies those whose figurative eyes are affected.
e: los ojos del corazón
This metaphor joins perception with the inner person: ‘the eyes of the heart.’ It is the grammatical subject placed after sean iluminados.

g: Exclamative cuán + adjective
‘Cuán incomparable es ...’ means ‘how incomparable ... is.’ Cuán intensifies the adjective and carries a written accent.
e: a favor de los que creemos
A favor de means ‘for the benefit of.’ Los que is a substantivized relative expression meaning ‘those who,’ here followed by creemos.

g: Cuando + completed past actions
‘Cuando lo resucitó ... y lo sentó’ coordinates two preterite verbs. In both clauses lo is the direct object referring to Cristo.
e: a su derecha
Sentar a alguien a la derecha means ‘seat someone at the right hand,’ a conventional position of honor and authority.

g: No solo ... sino también
‘No solo en este mundo, sino también en el venidero’ adds a second, stronger scope: ‘not only ... but also.’ Mundo is understood after venidero.
e: muy por encima de
This multiword preposition means ‘far above.’ Muy intensifies por encima de before the list of powers and titles.

g: Dar como + role noun
In ‘lo dio como cabeza,’ dar does not mean a simple physical transfer; como introduces the role in which Cristo was given to the church.
e: sometió todas las cosas al dominio de Cristo
Someter algo al dominio de alguien means ‘subject something to someone's rule.’ Al contracts a + el before dominio.

g: Demonstrative subject + explanatory relatives
‘Esta, que es su cuerpo’ uses esta to refer to la iglesia; the relative clause identifies it before the main predicate es la plenitud.
e: lo llena todo por completo
Spanish can combine the object pronoun lo with todo for an exhaustive object: ‘fills it all/everything.’ Por completo further reinforces totality.
